parts.title: Word List
parts.content:
Detailed Meanings

😎
amber[aembar]n.
Amber is a hard, yellowish material that comes from trees.
→ The necklace was made from pieces of amber.
😎
charcoal[tfaxkoul]n.
Charcoal is a black material that is used as fuel for fire.
→ There was burnt charcoal left on the ground from an old fire.
😎
columnist[kdlemnist]n.
A columnist is a writer who creates articles about a particular subject.
→ The columnist won praise for his articles about life on the farm.
😎
courteous[kairtias]adj.
When someone is courteous, they are polite and respectful.
→ The mother asked her family to be courteous to their guests.
😎
credentials[kridenfalz]n.
Credentials are the proof of someone’s experience or ability to do something.
→ The mechanic hung his credentials on his office wall.
😎
cricket[krikit]n.
A cricket is an insect that makes loud noises, usually at night.
→ In the country, we could see the stars and hear the crickets at night.
😎
delta[delta]n.
A delta is flat area where a river splits into smaller rivers that flow into the sea.
→ The archeologists found many ancient materials in the delta of the Nile River.
😎
detergent[dita:rd3ent]n.
Detergent is soap that is used to clean clothes or dishes.
→ My brother added too much detergent to the wash, and bubbles got all over the floor.
😎
euphemism[ju:famizam]n.
A euphemism is a term that is used in place of a mean or unpleasant word.
→ “Window maintenance officer” is a euphemism for a window washer.
😎
expire[ikspaiar]v.
To expire is to no longer be effective because its use has come to an end.
→ The man’s driver’s license was going to expire in two days.
😎
granite[graenit]n.
Granite is a very hard type of rock that is often black or pink.
→ The kitchen counter was made of granite.
😎
gravel[graeval]n.
Gravel is a combination of small stones mixed with sand.
→ The ground around the swing set was covered with gravel.
😎
haunt[ho:nt]v.
To haunt is to cause problems or negative thoughts over a long period of time.
→ His thoughts about his scary dream haunted him for weeks.
😎
liberal[liberal]adj.
When someone is liberal, they accept different ideas and people.
→ My grandparents aren’t as liberal as my parents.
😎
maze[meiz]n.
A maze is a system of paths that is complicated and easy to get lost in.
→ We got lost in the maze in the garden.
😎
moss[mo(:)s]n.
Moss is a small green or yellow plant that grows on wet dirt, rocks, or tree trunks.
→ Be careful not to slip on the moss that’s covering those rocks.
😎
pebble[pebal]n.
A pebble is a small, round stone.
→ We threw pebbles into the lake to make the water splash.
😎
peck[pek]v.
When a bird pecks, it bites or hits something with its beak.
→ The birds pecked at the seeds on the ground.
😎
reservoir[rezervwa:/-]n.
A reservoir is a place for storing water for a town to use.
→ If it doesn’t rain soon, the reservoir is going to dry up completely.
😎
streak[stri:k]n.
A streak is a long, thin mark that is easy to see.
→ Her hair was brown except for a streak which she dyed blonde.

sections.title: Exercise 2: Write a word that is similar in meaning to the underlined part.

questions.content: 1. After seeing her house on fire, jenna <u>was troubled by thoughts of fire.</u>
questions.explanation: haunt (v): to cause problems or negative thoughts over a long period of time.

questions.content: 2. The boy <u>had small round</u> rocks stuck on the bottom of his shoe.
questions.explanation: pebble (n): a small, round stone.

questions.content: 3. The bird <u>bit or hit the dish and</u> carried away pieces of bread.
questions.explanation: peck (v): to bite or hit something with a beak.

questions.content: 4. The city made <u>a place to store water, so there</u> would always be water for the people.
questions.explanation: reservoir (n): a place for storing water for a town to use.

questions.content: 5. She poured <u>soap to clean dishes</u> into the sink and washed the dishes.
questions.explanation: detergent (n): soap that is used to clean clothes or dishes.

questions.content: 6. The woman was impressed by her friend’s <u>polite and respectful</u> brother.
questions.explanation: courteous (adj): polite and respectful.

questions.content: 7. The scientist went to school for many years to earn <u>her proof of ability.</u>
questions.explanation: credentials (n): the proof of someone’s experience or ability.

questions.content: 8. I added some more <u>rocks that served as fuel to the fire.</u>
questions.explanation: charcoal (n): a black material that is used as fuel for fire.

questions.content: 9. Clara didn’t want to offend her grandmother, so <u>she used a replacement for an unpleasant word</u> to refer to old age.
questions.explanation: euphemism (n): a term that is used in place of a mean or unpleasant word.

questions.content: 10. The land in the <u>flat place where the river divides was good for growing</u> food.
questions.explanation: delta (n): flat area where a river splits into smaller rivers that flow into the sea.

parts.title: Comprehensive Reading
parts.content:
The Mad Hatter

One morning, Lucas sat outside with his grandfather. They looked past the gravel road that led to a natural reservoir on the delta. On the other side of the water, there was a cottage.

“ Does a ghost live there?” Lucas asked.

“ No, a mad hatter lives there,” said his grandfather. Lucas didn’t know what a mad hatter was, but the image of a scary man haunted him.

Later, Lucas went for a walk in the forest. He collected pieces of amber and granite that he found on the ground. He looked at the moss on the trees and watched a bird peck at the ground. But the forest was like a maze. Soon, Lucas was lost.

Lucas heard somebody behind him. He wanted to run away, but he fell. He had a streak of blood on his shirt and some pebbles stuck in his skin. Then a man appeared.

“ I will take you home. First, let’s get you cleaned up,” he said.

Lucas followed him. When they arrived at the cottage, he realized the man was the mad hatter!

He sat down inside. It smelled like charcoal, but it looked like a normal house. The man brought Lucas back some medicine.

“ It’s a bit old, but it’s not expired,” the man said.

While Lucas cleaned his cut, the man washed the blood out of his shirt with detergent.

Lucas asked, “Are you a mad hatter?”

The man laughed and replied, “That’s a euphemism for a crazy person. Actually, I’m pretty normal. I’m a columnist fora newspaper,” said the man. He pointed to his credentials which hung on the wall.

Lucas could hear the crickets outside. It was getting dark, so he asked, “ Could you take me home now?”

The man said yes. Lucas was surprised that people thought the man was crazy. He was actually very courteous. Maybe Lucas should have a more liberal attitude. Next time, Lucas wouldn’t make judgments about people without getting to know them first.

sections.title: Part A: Mark each statement T for true or F for false.

questions.content: 1. Lucas’s thoughts about the house across the reservoir haunted him.
questions.explanation: Câu này ĐÚNG. Cuối đoạn 3 có ghi: "Lucas didn’t know what a mad hatter was, but the image of a scary man haunted him." (Lucas không biết thợ làm mũ điên là gì, nhưng hình ảnh một người đàn ông đáng sợ cứ ám ảnh cậu). Do đó những suy nghĩ về ngôi nhà khiến cậu bị ám ảnh.

questions.content: 2. Lucas collected crickets and moss while he walked through the forest.
questions.explanation: Câu này SAI. Theo đoạn 4: "He collected pieces of amber and granite that he found on the ground." (Cậu bé thu nhặt những mẩu hổ phách và đá granite tìm thấy trên mặt đất), chứ không phải thu nhặt dế (crickets) và rêu (moss).

questions.content: 3. The bird was pecking at the maze.
questions.explanation: Câu này SAI. Đoạn 4 viết: "...and watched a bird peck at the ground." (...và nhìn một con chim mổ xuống mặt đất), không phải mổ vào mê cung (maze).

questions.content: 4. Lucas got a streak of blood on his shirt and pebbles in his skin from falling down.
questions.explanation: Câu này ĐÚNG. Đoạn 5 có miêu tả: "He wanted to run away, but he fell. He had a streak of blood on his shirt and some pebbles stuck in his skin." (Cậu bé muốn bỏ chạy, nhưng lại bị ngã. Cậu có một vệt máu trên áo và vài viên sỏi găm vào da).

questions.content: 5. The man’s house smelled like food that had expired.
questions.explanation: Câu này SAI. Trong đoạn 8 có nhắc tới: "It smelled like charcoal, but it looked like a normal house." (Nó có mùi giống như than củi, nhưng trông giống một ngôi nhà bình thường). Ngôi nhà có mùi than củi chứ không phải mùi thức ăn hết hạn.

questions.content: 1. Where was the cottage located in relation to the grandfather’s house?
options: It was located past the gravel road and on the other side of the natural reservoir on the delta.
It was in the middle of a dark forest filled with moss.
It was on top of a mountain made of granite.
It was next to a large maze.
questions.explanation: Ở đoạn 1 có miêu tả: "They looked past the gravel road that led to a natural reservoir on the delta. On the other side of the water, there was a cottage." (Họ nhìn qua con đường rải sỏi dẫn đến một hồ chứa nước tự nhiên trên đồng bằng châu thổ. Ở phía bên kia mặt nước, có một ngôi nhà nhỏ). Do đó đáp án A là chính xác.

questions.content: 2. What did the man wash Lucas’s shirt with?
options: He washed it with water from the reservoir.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 10 viết rất rõ: "While Lucas cleaned his cut, the man washed the blood out of his shirt with detergent." (Trong khi Lucas rửa vết thương, người đàn ông đã giặt sạch vết máu trên áo cậu bằng bột giặt). Đáp án A là đúng.

questions.content: 3. Why did the man point to his credentials on the wall?
options: To prove that he was a columnist.
To show that he was a mad hatter.
To prove that he was a doctor.
To show that he owned the cottage.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 12 kể lại: "Actually, I’m pretty normal. I’m a columnist for a newspaper,” said the man. He pointed to his credentials which hung on the wall." ("Thật ra, chú khá bình thường. Chú là người phụ trách chuyên mục cho một tờ báo," người đàn ông nói. Ông chỉ vào các chứng chỉ nghề nghiệp của mình treo trên tường). Điều này chứng minh ông ấy là một nhà báo, do đó đáp án A đúng.

questions.content: 4. What did the man say about the term “ mad hatter” ?
options: He said it was a euphemism for a crazy person.
He said it was his real name.
He said it meant he loved making hats.
He said it was a word for a very courteous person.
questions.explanation: Cũng trong đoạn 12, ông giải thích: "That’s a euphemism for a crazy person." (Đó là một lối nói hoa mỹ/uyển ngữ để chỉ một kẻ điên). Đáp án A là chính xác.

questions.content: 5. What did the courteous man teach Lucas at the end of the story?
options: He should have a more liberal attitude and not judge people without getting to know them.
He taught him how to navigate out of the maze.
He taught him to be careful of birds that peck.
He taught him how to collect pebbles and amber.
questions.explanation: Ở đoạn cuối, Lucas rút ra bài học: "Maybe Lucas should have a more liberal attitude. Next time, Lucas wouldn’t make judgments about people without getting to know them first." (Có lẽ Lucas nên có một thái độ cởi mở hơn. Lần tới, Lucas sẽ không phán xét người khác mà chưa tìm hiểu họ trước). Đáp án A là câu trả lời đúng.
